# 1 Kings Chapter 12 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Rehoboam went to Shechem, where all Israel had gathered to make him king.

**2** When Jeroboam son of Nebat heard the news — he was still in Egypt, where he had fled from King Solomon — he returned from Egypt.

**3** The people sent for him, and Jeroboam and the whole assembly went to Rehoboam and said,

**4** "Your father crushed us with heavy labor. Lighten the harsh demands and the heavy burden he placed on us, and we will serve you."

**5** Rehoboam answered, "Come back in three days." So the people left.

**6** King Rehoboam consulted the older advisers who had served his father Solomon during his lifetime. "What do you recommend?" he asked.

**7** They replied, "If you will serve this people today — if you will be their servant, answer them well, and speak kindly to them — they will serve you forever."

**8** But Rehoboam rejected the advice of the elders and turned to the young men who had grown up with him and now served him.

**9** He asked them, "What do you suggest? How should we respond to these people who are asking me to lighten the burden my father put on them?"

**10** The young men who had grown up with him replied, "This is what you should tell them: 'My little finger is thicker than my father's waist!

**11** My father laid a heavy burden on you? I'll make it heavier! My father disciplined you with whips? I'll discipline you with barbed lashes!'"

**12** Three days later, Jeroboam and all the people returned to Rehoboam, as the king had instructed.

**13** The king answered the people harshly. Rejecting the advice of the elders,

**14** he spoke to them as the young men had advised: "My father made your burden heavy; I will make it heavier. My father disciplined you with whips; I will discipline you with barbed lashes."

**15** The king refused to listen to the people. This turn of events was from the LORD, to fulfill the word he had spoken to Jeroboam son of Nebat through Ahijah of Shiloh.

**16** When all Israel saw that the king refused to listen, the people shouted back: "What share do we have in David? We owe nothing to the son of Jesse! Go home, Israel! Look after your own house, David!" And the Israelites went home.

**17** But Rehoboam still ruled over the Israelites living in the towns of Judah.

**18** King Rehoboam sent Adoram, who was in charge of the forced labor, but all Israel stoned him to death. King Rehoboam barely escaped by jumping into his chariot and racing back to Jerusalem.

**19** And Israel has been in rebellion against the house of David ever since.

**20** When all Israel heard that Jeroboam was back, they summoned him to the assembly and made him king over all Israel. Only the tribe of Judah remained loyal to the house of David.

**21** When Rehoboam arrived in Jerusalem, he mobilized the entire fighting force of Judah and Benjamin — a hundred and eighty thousand warriors — to attack Israel and reclaim the kingdom.

**22** But God's word came to Shemaiah the man of God:

**23** "Tell Rehoboam son of Solomon, king of Judah, and all the people of Judah, Benjamin, and the rest of the nation:

**24** 'This is what the LORD says: Do not attack your fellow Israelites. Everyone go home, because I am behind this.'" They obeyed the LORD's word and went home.

**25** Jeroboam fortified Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim and made it his capital. He also fortified Penuel.

**26** But Jeroboam thought to himself, "The kingdom will eventually go back to David's house.

**27** If these people keep going up to the LORD's temple in Jerusalem to offer sacrifices, their loyalty will shift back to King Rehoboam of Judah. They'll kill me and return to him."

**28** After consulting his advisers, the king made two golden calves. He announced to the people, "You've been going to Jerusalem long enough! Here are your gods, Israel — the gods who brought you out of Egypt!"

**29** He set up one calf in Bethel and the other in Dan.

**30** And this became a terrible sin. The people traveled as far as Dan to worship before the calf there.

**31** Jeroboam also built shrines on the hilltops and appointed anyone he wanted as priests — people who were not Levites.

**32** He created a festival on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, imitating the festival in Judah, and offered sacrifices on the altar. He did this in Bethel, sacrificing to the calves he had made. He also stationed the priests he had appointed at the shrines in Bethel.

**33** On the fifteenth day of the eighth month — a date he chose on his own authority — he went up to the altar he had built in Bethel. He established his own festival for the Israelites and went to the altar to burn incense.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

1. **12:7 — "if you will be their servant"**: The elders offer the most profound leadership principle in the Bible: power flows to those who serve. Rehoboam's rejection of this advice costs him ten tribes. He wanted to be feared; the elders knew he needed to be trusted.

2. **12:15 — "this turn of events was from the LORD"**: The narrator pulls back the curtain: Rehoboam's stupidity is real, but it serves God's announced plan. Human folly and divine sovereignty operate simultaneously, without canceling each other out.

3. **12:16 — "What share do we have in David?"**: The kingdom splits along a fault line that runs all the way back to the tribal era. The old north-south tension — always present, temporarily suppressed by David and Solomon — erupts permanently. Unity lasted two generations.

4. **12:28 — "Here are your gods"**: These are Aaron's exact words at Sinai (Exodus 32:4). Jeroboam doesn't just commit idolatry — he deliberately reenacts the worst sin in Israel's memory and turns it into official worship. This is the "sin of Jeroboam" that the narrator will reference for the rest of Kings.

5. **12:33 — "a date he chose on his own authority"**: The narrator's final verdict: Jeroboam invents his own religious calendar. Unauthorized worship — worship on human terms instead of God's — becomes the northern kingdom's defining characteristic and the reason for its eventual destruction.

— PNEUMA
